## 2. Instructions requiring interpretation

The main six-stage workflow, schemas, category decision order, risk defaults, overlap handling, Windows UTF-8 advice, and output paths were clear. The following details required judgment.

### Navigation illustration

`references/evidence-extraction.md` says: “A navigation box (e.g. a sidebar listing related topics) may be extracted as `text`, with `location` saying `Navigation box`.” It also says to “skip menus” and “Skip page numbers, logos and decoration.” It does not explicitly distinguish an informational network illustration inside a navigation box from decoration.

I retained one optional navigation-label entry (EV-029) and one explicitly navigation-only illustration entry (EV-030). Neither supports any verdict or creates any omission. I skipped the Wikipedia header, revision banner, edit controls, top disambiguation note, and site links. A clearer instruction would say whether to omit navigation illustrations entirely.

### Mistaken adjective copied into a node label

`references/audit-rules.md` says: “Only the label, the definition and the relationship are audited.” It also says: “Judge the tree item against the more specific evidence: an explanation, a formula or a worked example outweighs a single word or a sweeping summary sentence.” It does not explicitly settle a node whose label repeats a mistaken source adjective while its definition accurately repeats the formula.

N014 is labelled “反对称符号函数” but correctly gives the source's piecewise formula with f(0)=+1. I prioritized the formula, marked the node supported, and included the zero-boundary conflict in its permitted source-problem note. I did not count the copied source adjective as a separate tree finding. This follows the specific-evidence rule; the treatment of the label is an interpretation worth making explicit in the skill.

### Omission grouping and significance

`references/audit-rules.md` says: “One entry per node or topic, not per sentence,” and also: “Background: one entry per kind in each section ... the other names given in a section are one entry, even for several concepts.” It says supporting-detail and background omissions are reported “always.”

I used the section-specific background rule for external names and structure aliases, even when a group concerns more than one node. I grouped the long history into one history-background omission and kept its letter-recognition application/limitation as a separate background kind. I counted named learning methods as core omissions and aliases/proof attribution as supporting omissions. The resulting 14 omissions include 10 supporting details; their count should not be read as 14 substantive errors.

The single-layer limitation required a significance judgment: N031 gives XOR as an example and N030 states a convergence limitation, but no node explicitly states the source's general representational limitation. I reported the latter as one core omission, rather than treating the example or lack of convergence guarantee as a complete statement of it.

### Source wording for R

`references/audit-rules.md` says a claim attributed to the source is a conceptual error when the source states it differently, and says: “A slip that only outside knowledge reveals is not evident.” SKILL.md requires suspected outside explanations to be marked “资料外释义，待核实.”

I treated N029 as a source-attribution mismatch: “最大范数” differs from the printed “最大平均值.” I did not assert that the tree's mathematical interpretation is false or silently replace the source with it. The recommendation preserves the correct transcribed bound, flags the source wording as a possible slip, and marks the tree's interpretation as outside the supplied material and awaiting verification. This part was resolved by the existing rules, not external research.

## 3. Image-reading method and limitations

I read all six original 800×600 JPEGs using `functions.exec` with `tools.view_image`. I used local Pillow commands to make 2× enlarged working copies of every page, then viewed those copies with the same tool. This was visual reading; no OCR service, browser, web search, or external article text was used.

Small Chinese text, superscripts, subscripts, strict versus non-strict inequalities, and screenshots overlapping at paragraph boundaries needed close reading. I compared consecutive pages, extracted each statement once on its first complete appearance, and kept formulas linearized in Unicode with their conditions and index ranges. The criterion formula appears on page 5 with its introductory sentence; that sentence also begins at the end of page 4. Pages 5 and 6 repeat most of the learning algorithm, so repeated material was not extracted twice.

Before making the exact-word findings, I made and re-read dedicated crops of page 5's α interval and page 6's convergence/R wording. They confirm `0 < α ≤ 1` and “最大平均值.” Working enlargements and crops are in `work/`.

The tiny anatomical labels inside page 1's neuron illustration remained unreadable at 2×. I recorded EV-013 as `low` certainty with `［无法辨认］`; it supports no rejection or omission. The caption and the surrounding readable anatomy text were extracted separately at high certainty. No hidden labels were filled in from general knowledge.

The article's two output conventions, 0/1 and ±1, were retained separately. Zero-boundary checks against the printed formulas identify the source's “反对称” and strictly-positive-term claims as source issues. The phrase defining R is reported as a possible source slip only, because the supplied pages do not establish an alternative definition.
